title: Treaty of Portsmouth
summary: The treaty signed on 5 September 1905 at the naval yard at Kittery, Maine, ended the Russo-Japanese War. Russia recognised Japan's paramountcy in Korea and gave up the Liaodong lease, the South Manchuria Railway and the southern half of Sakhalin; Theodore Roosevelt, who had mediated, took the Nobel Peace Prize for it. It is in the atlas as the first occasion on which an Asian power defeated a European empire in a war and was conceded the spoils at a European-style congress, a fact read at the time — in Constantinople and in Peking as much as in Tokyo — as evidence that the arrangement of the world was not fixed.
